hypotheses.statement: A typed pressure-aware adaptive recurrence controller can match the task success of a sufficiently deep fixed recurrence budget while using materially less compute on heterogeneous episode regimes.
hypotheses.mechanism: Continue expensive recurrent processing only while unresolved pressure remains material and the estimated marginal verified benefit of another recurrence exceeds compute/resource/instability cost; use multi-step trend/patience so productive cycles are not misclassified as failure.
hypotheses.falsifier: On matched frozen H1 FRANK episodes, adaptive routing fails to achieve a Pareto improvement over fixed budgets in outcome-versus-compute/latency, or its advantage disappears under OOD tasks/regimes.

hypotheses.statement: Residual unresolved pressure is necessary to distinguish convergence from stagnation; low state delta alone is an unsafe halt criterion.
hypotheses.mechanism: A low-delta state can represent either successful contraction or a stalled attractor. The controller therefore needs both state-change and unresolved-pressure/error signals.
hypotheses.falsifier: A delta-only criterion matches pressure-aware routing on false-halt, task outcome, correction time and compute across frozen real H1 episodes.

hypotheses.statement: A multi-step trend/patience window is required to preserve productive limit-cycle-like recurrence that contains locally adverse or low-improvement steps.
hypotheses.mechanism: Useful recurrent computation may require an integration/organization step before a subsequent pressure reduction; one-step monotonic improvement is therefore too restrictive.
hypotheses.falsifier: One-step marginal-gain halting performs equivalently or better on validated productive-cycle H1 traces without increasing overthinking or compute.

hypotheses.statement: GWT ignition/focus can be useful as a recurrent-compute admission/continuation signal only when bound to objective episode/readout receipts; ignition/focus alone is not a sufficient halt/continue oracle.
hypotheses.mechanism: Workspace selection indicates prioritized global use, but continuation quality depends on downstream receiver use, residual pressure, outcomes, re-entry and cost shadows.
hypotheses.falsifier: A focus-only router equals or exceeds the receipt-bound controller under matched frozen episodes and shuffled-focus controls.

hypotheses.statement: Typed local recurrence controllers will outperform a single global stability threshold when FRANK loop families have heterogeneous timescales and productive dynamics.
hypotheses.mechanism: Perception, workspace, memory, goals, consolidation and other loops have different natural periods, noise and costs; one global threshold risks premature halt in slow loops or over-computation in fast loops.
hypotheses.falsifier: A single global controller matches or beats per-loop calibrated controllers on OOD outcome, false halt, instability, compute and recovery across loop families.

counterhypotheses.statement: Conventional persistent event-driven orchestration with fixed or externally scheduled budgets is sufficient; recurrent-control mathematics and GWT routing add little practical value.
counterhypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare fixed/event-driven scheduler against adaptive GWT-linked router using identical frozen episodes, seeds, model outputs and compute accounting.

counterhypotheses.statement: GWT focus is correlated with difficulty but adds no independent predictive or causal value beyond residual pressure and local controller state.
counterhypotheses.discriminating_test: Ablate focus, shuffle focus across matched episodes and compare incremental prediction/calibration of useful additional recurrence.

counterhypotheses.statement: Adaptive halting introduces routing overhead, synchronization cost and instability that erase theoretical compute savings on the Ubuntu runtime.
counterhypotheses.discriminating_test: Measure wall-clock latency, scheduler overhead, cache effects and tail latency, not only recurrence-count/FLOP proxies.

counterhypotheses.statement: The synthetic proxy advantage is an artifact of authored dynamics and thresholds and does not transfer to real FRANK episodes.
counterhypotheses.discriminating_test: Pre-register controller thresholds or fit only on training traces, then evaluate frozen held-out and OOD H1 traces.

counterhypotheses.statement: Adaptive compute can create shallow-halt attractors that systematically under-compute hard cases.
counterhypotheses.discriminating_test: Stress initial router bias/calibration, hard-example distribution shift and recovery/probe-budget behavior; compare against deep-start and fixed-depth controls.

promotion_guard: No hypothesis is promoted from this run. The executable evidence is synthetic proxy evidence only; current architecture implications are candidate constraints and H1 test requirements.
